security_annotations.description: Action "getsentry/action-github-app-token" uses mutable ref "v2" instead of a SHA pin. A compromised action version can inject malicious code into the workflow.
Action "actions/checkout" uses mutable ref "v4" instead of a SHA pin. A compromised action version can inject malicious code into the workflow.
Action "actions/checkout" uses mutable ref "v4" instead of a SHA pin. A compromised action version can inject malicious code into the workflow.
Action "actions-js/push" uses mutable ref "v1.5" instead of a SHA pin. A compromised action version can inject malicious code into the workflow.

Workflow "Helm Chart Validation" has no top-level permissions block. Without explicit permissions, the GITHUB_TOKEN gets default permissions which may be overly broad (write access to contents, packages, etc.).

Workflow "RHAI on XKS Chart E2E Test" uses pull_request_target trigger and job "upgrade-test", Checkout checks out fork code (ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}). This allows arbitrary code from a fork PR to run with write access to the base repo's secrets and GITHUB_TOKEN.

Workflow "RHAI on XKS Chart E2E Test" uses pull_request_target trigger and job "e2e-test", Checkout checks out fork code (ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}). This allows arbitrary code from a fork PR to run with write access to the base repo's secrets and GITHUB_TOKEN.
